steps.body: A graph's SHAPE tells a story even without numbers. Going UP means the output is increasing; going DOWN means decreasing; FLAT means staying the same. Steeper means changing faster.

widget.prompt: A distance-vs-time graph is FLAT (horizontal) for a while. What's happening?

segments.label: A
segments.meaning: The output increases at a constant rate.

choices.label: Not moving — distance stays the same
choices.feedback: Right — a flat graph means the output (distance) isn't changing: standing still.

choices.label: Moving faster and faster
choices.feedback: That would be a graph curving upward more steeply, not a flat line.

choices.label: Moving at a steady speed
choices.feedback: Steady speed is a straight SLANTED line — flat means not moving at all.

choices.label: Moving backward
choices.feedback: Moving backward would slope DOWN — a flat line means no movement.

widget.successFeedback: Right — a flat graph means the output (distance) isn't changing: standing still.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.

steps.body: A steeper section means the output changes faster there. On a distance-vs-time graph, a steep climb is fast movement and a gentle climb is slow movement. Reading steepness reads speed.

explanationVariants: A steeper part of a distance-time graph means moving FASTER there.
Steeper slope = faster rate of change = faster movement.

widget.prompt: On a distance-vs-time graph, one section is much STEEPER than the rest. What does that mean?

segments.label: A
segments.meaning: The output increases at a slower constant rate.

segments.label: B
segments.meaning: The output increases at a faster constant rate.

choices.label: Moving faster during that section
choices.feedback: Right — steeper means a bigger rate of change: faster movement.

choices.label: Moving slower during that section
choices.feedback: Steeper means FASTER, not slower — a gentle slope would be slow.

choices.label: Standing still during that section
choices.feedback: Standing still is a FLAT section — steep means fast movement.

choices.label: Turning around during that section
choices.feedback: Turning around would slope downward — steep upward means fast forward movement.

widget.successFeedback: Right — steeper means a bigger rate of change: faster movement.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.

widget.prompt: A graph rises steadily, then goes flat. What's the story?

segments.label: Rising part
segments.meaning: The output climbs steadily — something is increasing at a constant rate.

segments.label: Flat part
segments.meaning: The output stops changing — it holds steady at its value.

choices.label: The story
choices.feedback: For example: a car drives at steady speed (rising distance), then parks (flat distance).

widget.successFeedback: Right — the shape maps directly onto the story: steady increase, then holding steady.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Read the rising stage first and the flat stage second; the graph order is the story order.

explanationVariants: A graph sloping DOWN means the output is decreasing over time.
A downward slope shows the value falling.

widget.prompt: A temperature-vs-time graph slopes DOWNWARD. What's happening to the temperature?

segments.label: A
segments.meaning: The output decreases at a constant rate.

choices.label: It's decreasing over time
choices.feedback: Right — a downward slope means the output (temperature) is falling.

choices.label: It's increasing over time
choices.feedback: Increasing would slope UP — a downward slope means it's falling.

choices.label: It's staying constant
choices.feedback: Constant is a FLAT line — a downward slope means decreasing.

choices.label: It's rising then falling
choices.feedback: Rising then falling would go up then down — a steady downward slope is just decreasing.

widget.successFeedback: Right — a downward slope means the output (temperature) is falling.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.

explanationVariants: A graph that rises but flattens out is increasing more and more SLOWLY — the rate of change is shrinking.
Flattening while still rising means slowing growth.

widget.prompt: A graph keeps rising but gets less and less steep (flattening out). What does this show?

segments.label: A
segments.meaning: The output still increases, but more and more slowly.

choices.label: Still increasing, but more and more slowly
choices.feedback: Right — rising means increasing; flattening means the rate of change is shrinking.

choices.label: Decreasing steadily
choices.feedback: It's still RISING (increasing) — just more slowly; decreasing would slope down.

choices.label: Increasing faster and faster
choices.feedback: Getting less steep means SLOWING down, not speeding up.

choices.label: Staying completely flat
choices.feedback: It's still rising, just gently — a completely flat graph wouldn't rise at all.

widget.successFeedback: Right — rising means increasing; flattening means the rate of change is shrinking.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.

steps.body: Match graph sections to a bike ride.
explanationVariants: Steep up = pedaling fast; gentle up = pedaling slowly; flat = stopped; down = coasting back. Match each shape to its action.
Each shape maps to an action: steepness is speed, flat is stopped, down is returning.

widget.prompt: On a distance-from-home vs. time graph for a bike ride, which section shows the rider STOPPED to rest?

segments.label: A
segments.meaning: The output increases at a faster constant rate.

segments.label: C
segments.meaning: The output increases at a slower constant rate.

segments.label: D
segments.meaning: The output decreases at a constant rate.

choices.label: A flat (horizontal) section
choices.feedback: Right — flat means distance isn't changing: the rider is stopped.

choices.label: A steep upward section
choices.feedback: Steep upward means riding away fast — not stopped.

choices.label: A gentle upward section
choices.feedback: Gentle upward means riding away slowly — still moving, not stopped.

choices.label: A downward section
choices.feedback: Downward means heading back toward home — moving, not stopped.

widget.successFeedback: Right — flat means distance isn't changing: the rider is stopped.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.

hints: Stopped means the distance from home isn't changing.
On the graph, 'not changing' shows up as a flat, horizontal section.
So the flat section is where the rider stopped to rest.

steps.body: A graph's shape encodes the story: direction, steepness, and flatness all mean something.
takeaways: Up = increasing, down = decreasing, flat = unchanging.
Steeper = changing faster; gentler = changing slower.
A rising graph that flattens is still increasing, just more slowly.

concept.body: A graph's shape tells a story: up = increasing, down = decreasing, flat = unchanging, and steeper = changing faster.

explanationVariants: A flat (horizontal) graph means the output isn't changing.
Flat means no change — the value holds steady.

widget.prompt: What does a FLAT (horizontal) section of a graph mean?

choices.label: The output is not changing
choices.feedback: Right — flat means the value holds steady.

choices.label: The output is increasing fast
choices.feedback: Increasing fast is a STEEP upward line — flat means no change.

choices.label: The output is decreasing
choices.feedback: Decreasing slopes DOWN — flat means unchanging.

choices.label: The graph has ended
choices.feedback: A flat section is still part of the graph — it just shows no change.

widget.successFeedback: Right — flat means the value holds steady.
widget.explorationFeedback: Read the graph from left to right, then choose the claim supported by its direction, steepness, flatness, or curvature.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Use the visible graph shape and the axis labels together; do not infer from color alone.
